title: U.S. House · Virginia's 6th District
area: Western and central Virginia's Shenandoah Valley and Roanoke region, including Winchester, Harrisonburg, Staunton, Lexington, Roanoke and Botetourt County.

context.text: Both primaries were canceled after only one candidate qualified for each ballot line. On the Democratic side, Wendy Gooditis, Ken Mitchell, Hugh Murray and Pete Barlow withdrew or were disqualified, leaving Beth Macy unopposed for the nomination. Incumbent Benjamin Lee Cline advanced unopposed on the Republican line. Cook Political Report, Decision Desk, Inside Elections and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rate the race Solid/Safe Republican as of September 22, 2026.

candidates.name: Benjamin Lee Cline
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed after the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Ben Cline is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Virginia's 6th District, seeking a fifth term. A Virginia attorney who began his career on the staff of Rep. Bob Goodlatte, he served 16 years in the Virginia House of Delegates and worked as an assistant Commonwealth's attorney before winning the seat Goodlatte vacated in 2018. He sits on the Judiciary, Appropriations, Intelligence and Budget committees.

background.text: Born in Stillwater, Oklahoma, in 1972. His official biography says he grew up in Rockbridge County, Virginia, and graduated from Lexington High School in 1990.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Bates College in 1994 and a J.D. from the University of Richmond in 2007.
Began working for Rep. Bob Goodlatte on his legislative staff in 1994 and ultimately served as his Chief of Staff; Ballotpedia lists this service as 1994 to 2002.
Served as president of New Dominion Solutions LLC from 2002 to 2007, according to Ballotpedia.
Served in the Virginia House of Delegates for the 24th District from 2002 to 2018, where he chaired the Committee on Militia, Police, and Public Safety.
Worked as an attorney in private practice and was an Assistant Commonwealth's Attorney for Rockingham County and the City of Harrisonburg from 2007 to 2013.

Won the open 6th District seat in 2018 to succeed Goodlatte and took office January 3, 2019. In the current Congress he is a member of the House Judiciary, Appropriations, Permanent Select Intelligence and Budget committees.
According to his official biography, he lives in Botetourt County with his wife, Elizabeth, and their two daughters.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary.
Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations.
Serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.
Serves on the House Committee on the Budget.

candidates.name: Beth Macy
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed after other candidates withdrew and the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Beth Macy is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Ben Cline for Virginia's 6th District. A longtime Roanoke Times reporter and best-selling author whose books include Factory Man, Dopesick and Paper Girl, she has not previously held elected office. She describes her campaign as focused on affordable health care, strong schools and rural communities.

background.text: Grew up in Urbana, Ohio, the daughter of a factory worker and a housepainter, according to Wikipedia; her campaign website says she grew up poor in a small Ohio town and was the first in her family to go to college.
Earned a bachelor's degree in journalism from Bowling Green State University in 1986 and a master's degree in creative writing from Hollins University in 1993, according to Wikipedia.
Spent 25 years as a reporter for The Roanoke Times, according to her campaign website, and settled in Roanoke, where she and her husband raised two children.
Awarded a Nieman Fellowship at Harvard University in 2010 and a Guggenheim Fellowship for general nonfiction in 2023, according to Wikipedia.

Author of Factory Man (2014), Truevine (2016), Dopesick (2018), Raising Lazarus (2022) and Paper Girl (2025). Her campaign website says Dopesick was adapted into an Emmy- and Peabody-winning Hulu series that she helped produce and write.
Announced her candidacy for the 6th District on November 18, 2025; the Democratic primary was canceled and she advanced as the nominee. She has not previously held elected office.

priorities.text: Making life affordable for working families and expanding access to health and mental health care.

Regulating data centers and artificial intelligence, including a proposed nationwide moratorium on new data centers until energy, environmental, cost and workforce concerns are addressed, and requiring Big Tech to pay the full costs of data-center construction and energy/water use.
priorities.quote: A nationwide moratorium on new data centers should be enforced until energy, environmental, cost, workforce and other citizens' concerns are addressed through legislation.

priorities.text: Protecting Social Security, Medicare and veterans' benefits from privatization, and raising the cap on Social Security payroll taxes so higher earners pay more into the system.

positions.summary: Says Congress should raise the cap on Social Security payroll taxes so wealthier earners pay a larger share.
Campaign priorities include expanding access to health and mental health care and opposing privatization of Medicare.
Calls for ending tariffs, saying they act as a tax on purchased goods and hurt farmers by shutting them out of overseas markets and raising equipment costs.

researchNotes: Cline did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and his campaign site (bencline.com) returned a bot-check page, so his current-cycle priorities in his own words could not be verified; the record items reflect his official committee assignments only.
